issues.description: Class UniqueTable constructor signature differs between template and solution and conflicts with its use in the template: In template repository (template_repository/dd.py) UniqueTable.__init__ is defined as def __init__(self, size: int) -> None:, but later the template instantiates UT = UniqueTable() with no argument (template_repository/dd.py). In the solution (solution_repository/dd.py) UniqueTable.__init__ is defined as def __init__(self) -> None:. The mismatch (required parameter in template but no-arg instantiation) will raise a TypeError when importing or running the template and therefore blocks students from running tests or building on the template.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template UniqueTable constructor signature consistent with its usage and the solution. The simplest fix is to change the template constructor to a no-argument initializer (def __init__(self) -> None:) and remove the unused 'size' parameter, matching the solution. Alternatively, make the parameter optional with a default (def __init__(self, size: int | None = None):) or change the UT instantiation to pass a size argument, but prefer aligning the template with the solution's no-arg constructor to avoid confusing students.
